subject: ventures/wedding-flower-order-optimizer
professional: a working wedding florist who buys wholesale (bunch/box packs) and quotes events; first checks that stem counts, pack rounding and cost match what the wholesaler would invoice, then whether minimum orders, delivery and per-flower waste are handled

evidence.correctness: Ran node --test '*.test.mjs' in the venture dir: 19 pass, 0 fail. Recomputed by hand, then ran analyze(EXAMPLE_FLOWERS, EXAMPLE_SHARED): (1) garden roses 96 stems +10% = 105.6 -> 106 to cover; packs 10@38 / 25@85; I enumerated b=0..5 big boxes and found 4 boxes + 1 bunch = 110 stems at $378 (b=2: $398, b=3: $407, b=0: $418); tool gave 1 x10 + 4 x25 = 110 stems, $378, 4 spare. Match. (2) spray roses 72 -> 79.2 -> 80; 2 x 40 @ $64 = $128 vs 8 bunches $152 vs 1 box + 4 bunches $140; tool $128, 0 spare. Match. (3) peonies 33 -> 36.3 -> 37; 8 x 5 @ $29 = $232, 3 spare. Match. Totals 378+168+83+128+232 = 989; small-pack-only 1069, saving 80; 989/2400 = 41.2%: match. Edge probes: 100 stems at 10% -> 110 and 70 at 30% -> 91 (float guard works); 10.5 stems -> 11; pack B smaller than pack A handled. Not recomputed against a second tool or a real wholesaler invoice.
evidence.completeness: README claims checked: up to 15 flowers (MAX_FLOWERS=15, page test checks 15 rows of inputs); two-pack mix tried exhaustively (works); spare stems and value (works); saving over small pack only (works); cost as share of budget (works, 41.2% on the example); CSV download (toCsv tested for header, rows, total). All claimed features exist and ran. No stubs or TODOs found. Not claimed and absent: minimum order value, delivery fee, per-flower waste.
evidence.verification: node --test: 19/19 pass. calc.test.mjs checks bestOrder against a brute-force grid, rounding, the damage allowance, bad rows. Mutations (each reverted with git checkout, git status clean): (A) maxB ceil->floor in bestOrder: CAUGHT (1 fail). (B) float guard sign on need ceil(stems*(1+loss/100) - 1e-9) -> +1e-9: CAUGHT (2 fail). (C) removed the documented tie-break 'fewer leftover stems on equal cost': SURVIVED, 7/7 pass, so the stated tie rule is untested. Brute-force oracle compares cost only, not stems or spare, so wrong spare counts on ties would pass. Float guard on percentages only exercised indirectly.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (84 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs, index.html script section. Pure, small, no dependencies, clear separation of calc and page, tests also lock the disclaimer and no-network claims. Defects: loss percent outside 0..100 or negative adds a warning but analysis still proceeds with the bad value and returns ok:true (calc.mjs analyze), so a warning can be missed; field 'naive' (no-damage small-pack cost) is computed and never used in totals or CSV (dead field); a flower row with stems but a non-numeric size silently yields NaN-driven warning only; all money in floats (fine at this scale).
evidence.claims: Backed: free, in-browser, nothing uploaded (page.test.mjs asserts no fetch/XHR/sendBeacon and local-only imports); 'cheapest exact order' (brute-force test and my hand checks); disclaimer 'No warranty' and 'not legal, tax, accounting, compliance, or financial advice' present in README and page (page test); 'Not decided' section and 'placeholders, not any wholesaler's' prices on page. Not backed or defective: llms.txt links the tool to https://duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo/... which CLAUDE.md says is now only a redirect, while the README uses marisstella.app (stale canonical URL). FAQ says 'many florists aim for flowers to be around a third' of client price with no source, while the tool's own example shows 41% with no comment. 'Ten percent is a common starting point' is unsourced. README says 'not legal, tax, accounting...' advice which is off-topic for a florist tool but harmless. I did not load the live page in a browser; checks were on file contents and tests.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job of a florist pricing a wedding: enter total stems per flower from recipes, set loss, enter bunch and case prices, read cheapest order. Works end to end for that single step in code (ran the example). Gaps a florist hits in the first hour: one global damage % for all flowers (peonies and ranunculus lose far more than eucalyptus; no per-flower override); no wholesaler minimum order or delivery fee, so a cheapest-by-stem order can still be unorderable; only two pack tiers (many wholesalers sell bunch, half-case, case); no stem-length/grade or substitutions; no way to enter a recipe, only a total (users must pre-sum bouquet recipes elsewhere); no saving or reload of the order across visits was checked. Ran in code only, not in a browser.
evidence.domain: Compared against normal wholesale florist practice (order in bunches of 5/10/25 or cases, add 10-15% for conditioning loss and breakage, buy to a case if cheaper, check minimums and delivery). Method of ceil(stems*(1+loss)) then minimum-cost mix of two pack sizes is sound and exact for what it models. Departures: uniform loss percent applied identically to every flower and rounded up once; spare stems are valued at the blended unit cost (reasonable); no unit-of-sale rules like case-only items or mixed-box restrictions; no allowance for buying spare focal flowers vs filler differently. A senior florist would accept the arithmetic but would not rely on it alone for a real order.

defects.what: One global damage allowance for all flowers; florists lose very different shares of roses, peonies, ranunculus and greenery, so the stems to cover are wrong per flower
No wholesaler minimum order value or delivery fee, so the 'cheapest order' may not be placeable; page only mentions this in prose
Tie-break rule (fewer leftover stems on equal cost) is untested: removing it passed all 7 calc tests; brute-force oracle compares cost only
llms.txt points at the old github.io address that now only redirects; README uses marisstella.app
Out-of-range damage percent only warns, then still computes with it and returns ok:true
Unsourced 'around a third' flower-cost rule in FAQ; unused 'naive' field computed per line

verdict: The arithmetic is right: three flower lines (roses $378, spray roses $128, peonies $232) and the totals ($989, $80 saving, 41.2%) recomputed by hand matched the tool exactly, 19 tests pass, and the code is small and clean. It does everything its README says. It falls short of the bar on claims (stale llms.txt URL, unsourced industry figures) and on domain/fitness: a single global loss percent, no minimum order or delivery handling, only two pack tiers. Verification is adequate but one of three seeded mutations (the documented tie-break) survived. By the computed rule correctness 3, claims 2, verification 3 means it does not meet the bar, but it is finished (completeness 3). Not tested in a live browser.
